surface_forms: notre ministre auprès du roi Théodose

appraisal_events.evidence: Accroché à moi, le professeur E… ne demandait qu'à ne pas me quitter... « Vous ne souffrez pas de cette hyperthermie ? »... « Ce qu'il faut, c'est éviter les sudations... »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's ironic concession that E… showed no satisfaction at being proven right is undercut by an extended satire of doctors' vanity and by E…'s own clumsy, jargon-laden, contradictory chatter and clinginess.

appraisal_events.evidence: ce n'était qu'à l'état de bien pâle reflet... la banalité d'un homme de dernier ordre... sa nullité intellectuelle surtout... un air d'une bête en cage, jetant... des regards qui exprimaient la peur, l'appétence et la stupidité... la même ardeur hystérique à le punir que jadis à le combler
appraisal_events.explanation: Vaugoubert is drawn as a pale, banal, intellectually null echo of Charlus's failings, and further undercut by a portrait of vain, fearful, hysterical behavior in both his aging vanity and his erratic patronage of a protégé.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Vaugoubert était un des meilleurs agents du Gouvernement français à l'étranger. Quand un homme prétendu supérieur... le remplaça plus tard, la guerre ne tarda pas à éclater
appraisal_events.explanation: Despite his personal absurdity, the narrator credits Vaugoubert with real professional competence as a diplomat, underscored by the war that broke out once an ostensibly superior successor replaced him.

status_effects.explanation: Continued comic diminishment through his clumsy jargon and clinginess, slightly tempered by the narrator's concession that he showed no satisfaction.
Explicit description as a pale, banal, unintelligent, hysterical version of Charlus's failings.
The comparison credits Charlus with real eloquence and biting wit, in contrast to Vaugoubert's banality, elevating him rhetorically even amid a passage about shared vice.
A separate, professional moment of the passage credits him with genuine competence as a diplomat, thrown into relief by the war that followed his replacement.
